speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me when it first appeared in relation to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is a classic "slapped cheek" sign. Do you have any history of sickle cell disease, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of the initial "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild constitutional symptoms, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease, caused by Parvovirus B19. Given the classic presentation, I am confident in this conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
